papers.title: Field Demonstration of Distributed Quantum Sensing without Post-Selection
papers.version: Phys. Rev. X 11,031009 version of record; original arXiv2011.02807v1 also inspected. Journal PDF checked by Astra and orchestrator.
papers.access: full journal PDF and initial preprint
papers.contribution: Entangled photons and coherent repeated phase sampling estimate a weighted combination of two separated phases without hiding lost photons through postselection.
papers.method: Telecom polarization-entangled pairs are delivered to two sensors; Bob samples his phase twice. Single and multiple detector events, heralding efficiencies and higher-order pair emissions enter photon-pass resource accounting. The SNL reference is an ideal lossless local estimation strategy with optimally allocated independent photon passes.
papers.result: Journal best 0.916 dB at 240 m; separate non-multipass result 0.326 dB. The 10 km random-phase measurement does not beat shot noise. [S70 p.5; Fig.3; Appendix E]
papers.limitations: Analysis: controlled waveplate phases and fibre spools do not demonstrate physical target sensing. Photon passes, including losses and multipair events, are counted; full infrastructure, acquisition time and alternative classical architectures are not the comparison metric. Journal additions take precedence over initial preprint values. [S70 pp.2–5; Appendices A–E]
papers.replication: Experimental apparatus, estimators and efficiency/resource derivation are documented in main text and appendicesA–C; no independent replication established in this bounded search. Raw public dataset/code not identified in examined preprint.
papers.data_code: Experimental apparatus, estimators and efficiency/resource derivation are documented in main text and appendicesA–C; no independent replication established in this bounded search. Raw public dataset/code not identified in examined preprint.
papers.conflicts: Not located in examined preprint; journal declaration not independently retrieved.
papers.relevance: Analysis: credible loss-aware network metrology mechanism for research on distributed sensing; no demonstrated defence sensing application.
papers.assessment: High confidence in scoped240m result; limited network scalability and operational relevance.

claims.text: At 240 m, best phase precision is 0.916 dB below the loss-accounted photon-pass shot-noise limit.
The non-multipass equal-weight phase experiment is 0.326 dB below its shot-noise limit.
The 10 km random-phase experiment does not beat the shot-noise limit because of losses.

papers.title: Distributed quantum sensing with mode-entangled spin-squeezed atomic states
papers.version: arxiv full manuscript; journal metadata cross-checked
papers.type: published journal study; reviewed preprint manuscript
papers.contribution: A shared quantum nondemolition measurement creates nonlocal entanglement between atomic modes, enabling differential clock and interferometer protocols.
papers.method: Rubidium ensembles in a common cavity are divided into as many as four spatial modes; a shared QND observation prepares correlated populations. Microwave Ramsey operations and Raman-pulse differential interferometry test the prepared modes. Each clock mode contains45000atoms. Baselines include projection-noise-limited coherent states and a projected mode-separable spin-squeezed network.
papers.result: Four-mode clock-network noise is11.6(1.1)dB below coherent-state QPN and4.5(0.8)dB below the projected mode-separable reference. The differential interferometer improves1.6(0.9)dB relative to its non-entangled counterpart; do not assign the clock-network gain to the interferometer.
papers.limitations: All nodes share laboratory cavity infrastructure; the atom modes are not a geographically separated clock network. The4.5dB reference is projected, not a separately field-operated competitor. Gains exploit improved squeezing efficiency as the total atom count entangled increases. Differential rejection of Raman common-mode phase noise is also present and must be separated from entanglement benefit. No broad optimized-classical end-to-end network comparison is demonstrated.
papers.replication: Full arxivv1 main text and Methods inspected; peer-reviewed title/date/DOI cross-checked on Nature landing page. Journal main text is paywalled; preprint-versus-final changes remain a version caveat. Journal data and analysis code are available from corresponding author upon reasonable request, not an open repository.
papers.data_code: Full arxivv1 main text and Methods inspected; peer-reviewed title/date/DOI cross-checked on Nature landing page. Journal main text is paywalled; preprint-versus-final changes remain a version caveat. Journal data and analysis code are available from corresponding author upon reasonable request, not an open repository.
papers.relevance: Analysis: a promising seam for differential gravity sensing and clock comparisons, requiring remote-node links and realistic interrogation cycles before defence interpretation becomes an observed application.
papers.assessment: High confidence in laboratory metrology; medium confidence in extrapolation beyond common apparatus.

papers.title: Entanglement-enhanced matter-wave interferometry in a high-finesse cavity
papers.access: full text and methods; supplement where provided
papers.contribution: Cavity-mediated entanglement is injected into a complete light-pulse matter-wave interferometer rather than demonstrated only as state preparation.
papers.method: Free-falling rubidium wave packets receive Raman momentum kicks in a high-finesse cavity. QND measurement and one-axis twisting prepare squeezed momentum states. The full Mach–Zehnder sequence uses OAT; phase noise and contrast define the Wineland parameter, with atom number and spatially varying coupling calibrated separately.
papers.result: For660(15)atoms the full interferometer has1.7±0.5dB enhancement beyond the calibrated SQL at evolution time0.112ms. Phase variance improves3.4(+0.9/−1.2)dB against the actual unsqueezed interferometer, which itself has imperfect contrast. Below-SQL sensitivity lasts less than0.7ms. Standalone squeezed-state gains are distinct.
papers.limitations: Short interrogation time and residual spin-related decoherence sharply limit practical inertial advantage. An independent unreviewed critique by McGuinness(arxiv2301.04396v2) disputes phase/SQL interpretation and resource accounting; its blanket denial is not established by citing it. Authors explicitly distinguish contrast-adjusted entanglement witness from larger ordinary noise cancellation. Independent calibrated acceleration-versus-phase and full-cycle comparisons would be more useful than accepting either universal claim.
papers.replication: Full corrected journal text and Methods read; public datasets at doi10.25810/t39m-c562 declared. Publisher correction(2022-12-06) restores omitted hbar labels and removes an incorrect peer-review-manuscript link, not a reported numerical-result retraction. Independent experimental replication not established.
papers.data_code: Full corrected journal text and Methods read; public datasets at doi10.25810/t39m-c562 declared. Publisher correction(2022-12-06) restores omitted hbar labels and removes an incorrect peer-review-manuscript link, not a reported numerical-result retraction. Independent experimental replication not established.
papers.conflicts: Authors declare no competing interests; NSF,DOE,NIST,DARPA funding listed.
papers.relevance: Analysis: directly relevant enabling physics for future inertial/gravity sensing; not a demonstrated navigation instrument or GNSS-denial test.
papers.assessment: High confidence in reported local calibrated laboratory variance/contrast; practical inertial superiority remains untested and critique warrants explicit parameter definition.

papers.title: Quantum locking of intrinsic spin squeezed state in Earth-field-range magnetometry
papers.access: full text and methods; supplement where provided
papers.contribution: Nonlinear Zeeman dynamics create intrinsic single-atom squeezing; optimized dynamical decoupling locks its changing axis to the observable instead of simply suppressing that dynamics.
papers.method: Breit–Rabi expansion yields a quadratic spin Hamiltonian. A differential-evolution algorithm chooses discretized RF rotation pulses. Numerical state fidelity and signal/noise propagation assess dark-interval and continuous-readout protocols; supplementary notes derive SQL and the nuclear-electron entanglement mechanism.
papers.result: Modelled87Rb maximum metrological gain approaches2.9dB. Under assumed1cm³ room-temperature cell,N=1.42e10 and10ms coherence, Discussion calculates4.29fT/sqrt(Hz) versus5.99fT/sqrt(Hz) CSS SQL and14.04fT/sqrt(Hz) NLZ-degraded reference. These are predictions, not recorded instrument sensitivity.
papers.limitations: Explicitly no atom–atom entanglement is needed; gain is single-atom nuclear-electron correlation and independent ofN. The largest apparent improvement also restores assumed coherence, not squeezing alone. Instantaneous-rotation and rotating-wave approximations constrain pulse duration. Readout backaction, gradients and measurement-duty trade-offs are discussed but no complete measured noise budget or moving-platform demonstration is supplied.
papers.replication: Main Results,Methods,Discussion and supplementary notes1–3,8 inspected. Equations and optimized pulse sequence are given; authors say evaluation data are within paper/supplement and additional data on request. No code repository identified; no experimental replication established because this is a proposed protocol.
papers.data_code: Main Results,Methods,Discussion and supplementary notes1–3,8 inspected. Equations and optimized pulse sequence are given; authors say evaluation data are within paper/supplement and additional data on request. No code repository identified; no experimental replication established because this is a proposed protocol.
papers.relevance: Analysis: a relevant control proposal for Earth-field sensing and potential magnetic navigation research; claimed operational sensitivity must await an experiment.
papers.assessment: High confidence in classification as numerical proposal; medium confidence in achievable hardware gain.

claims.text: Rb maximum modelled metrological gain approaches2.9dB.
No atom–atom entanglement appears; gain independent ofN.
4.29fT/sqrt(Hz) comes from assumed cell,atom number and coherence.

papers.title: Superabsorption in an organic microcavity: Toward a quantum battery
papers.version: arxiv full manuscript; journal metadata cross-checked
papers.type: published journal study; reviewed preprint manuscript
papers.contribution: Organic-molecule collective light–matter coupling produces faster absorption as absorber count increases; dephasing moves energy into less radiative dark modes.
papers.method: Lumogen-F Orange dye in polystyrene is placed between dielectric mirrors. Concentrations0.5%,1%,5%,10% span weak to strong coupling. Femtosecond pump–probe differential reflectivity is fit to an open-system model; peak population-derived energy density, rise time and charging power are extracted from model fits, with supporting spectroscopy and fit sensitivity in supplement.
papers.result: Spectroscopy supports superextensive charging and storage-capacity behaviour over tested regimes; scaling varies with coupling/decay regime. Only6–8% of initial pump energy enters the cavity according to reflectivity estimates. The observed energy is molecular excitation, not delivered electrical energy.
papers.limitations: This precursor has no demonstrated electrical extraction, useful discharge cycle or net wall-plug efficiency. Increased concentration and coupling regimes change together; fitted collective dynamics should not be reported as proof that entanglement uniquely causes practical energy advantage. Finite experimental concentration range, molecular quenching at larger concentration and dephasing/decay assumptions limit extrapolation. A fixed-resource comparison requires incident/absorbed energy,mode volume,loss and preparation accounting.
papers.replication: Full accessible arxiv PDF main text plus supplement examined; DOI/journal identity verified through opened publisher DOI and author university research portal. Version is latest downloadable arxiv manuscript, not an independently diffed journal PDF. Detailed fabrication,spectroscopy and fitting documented; independent replication/open code repository not established in this bounded review.
papers.data_code: Full accessible arxiv PDF main text plus supplement examined; DOI/journal identity verified through opened publisher DOI and author university research portal. papers.assessment: High confidence in spectroscopic collective enhancement; no demonstrated usable battery output.

papers.title: Superextensive electrical power from a quantum battery
papers.access: full text and methods; supplement where provided
papers.contribution: Charge-transport layers turn an organic polariton microcavity into a steady-state electrical-output device, addressing the missing extraction step in earlier spectroscopy-only battery demonstrations.
papers.method: Eight CuPc:C60 devices vary absorber count within a nominal126nm cavity. Cavity and no-cavity controls share substrates. Reflectance establishes strong coupling; ultrafast pump–probe data quantify excitation dynamics; current–voltage scans under625nm illumination measure electrical output. Intersystem crossing populates metastable triplet states; coupled-oscillator and open-system models connect these stages.
papers.result: Maximum electrical power density is roughly10–40microW/cm². The ratio of cavity/no-cavity peak power increases withN; authors interpret this as superextensive output, with modelPc~N². Optical excited-state signals persist tens of nanoseconds; the six-orders-of-magnitude ratio compares to charging times, not hours or years of storage.
papers.limitations: Always-illuminated steady-state photocurrent does not by itself demonstrate sustained useful dark discharge. Controls omit a metal mirror and therefore differ optically as well as in coupling; comparisons to an independently optimized photovoltaic architecture and equal absorbed/incident energy are needed for practical superiority. Concentration alters carrier dynamics,cavity detuning andQ; authors normalize with same-run controls and discussD8 deviation. No entanglement witness isolates uniquely quantum causal advantage. No complete round-trip/net external efficiency,macroscopic capacity or cycling durability demonstrated.
papers.replication: Full journal text,Methods and32-page supplement inspected, emphasizing geometry/controls,ultrafast normalization and electrical model. Data available on request; no public code repository identified. Independent replication not established.
papers.data_code: Full journal text,Methods and32-page supplement inspected, emphasizing geometry/controls,ultrafast normalization and electrical model. Data available on request; no public code repository identified. Independent replication not established.
papers.relevance: Analysis: worthwhile frontier test in low-light harvesting rather than evidence for near-term defence energy storage. Require dark-discharge energy,integrated photon-to-electric efficiency and optimized equal-resource classical controls.
papers.assessment: High confidence in measured electrical output; medium confidence in causal scaling interpretation; low deployment maturity.
